The ideal candidate will be: Interested in government, public policy, community engagement, and public higher education. Curious and eager to learn. Organized, dependable, and attentive to detail. A strong writer and communicator. Collaborative, professional, and highly responsive. Professional and responsive when interacting with external stakeholders. Able to take direction and increasingly assume responsibility as experience develops. Passionate about public higher education and community impact. Able to take direction and increasingly assume responsibility as experience develops. Adaptable, proactive, and solutions-oriented.

The Government Relations Specialist supports UC Irvine’s community and government relations activities, including stakeholder outreach, public policy research, government engagement, community partnerships, events, and office operations. Working under general supervision, the position assists senior staff in maintaining relationships with government officials, community organizations, business and civic leaders, and other external partners.

The successful candidate will have strong communication and organizational skills, an interest in public policy and higher education, and the ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
Community Relations & Partnership Development
Support outreach to community organizations, chambers of commerce, nonprofit organizations, business groups, neighborhood organizations, and other regional stakeholders.
Assist senior staff with maintaining community relationships and identifying opportunities for engagement.
Help coordinate community programs, meetings, events, and outreach activities.
Research community organizations, stakeholders, and regional issues relevant to UC Irvine.
Maintain stakeholder contact information and engagement records.
Participate in community meetings and events as assigned.
Government Relations & External Engagement
Support the office’s engagement with local, county, state, and federal elected officials, government agencies, and staff.
Track legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments relevant to UC Irvine.
Conduct research and prepare summaries of legislation, government actions, community issues, and policy developments.
Assist with advocacy activities and outreach related to institutional priorities.
Help coordinate campus visits, briefings, meetings, and events involving elected officials and government representatives.
Attend government, civic, and community meetings and provide summaries or follow-up information to senior staff.
Develop familiarity with public policy issues affecting higher education, healthcare, research, housing, economic development, and related areas.
Strategic Communications & Project Coordination
Draft and assist with briefing materials, correspondence, presentations, meeting summaries, reports, and stakeholder communications.
Conduct background research for meetings with government and community stakeholders.
Assist with planning public-facing events, town halls, community meetings, policy forums, and official visits.
Track projects, deadlines, stakeholder engagement, and follow-up activities.
Provide project coordination for initiatives led by the Office of Community & Government Relations.
Work collaboratively with campus colleagues on outreach and engagement activities.
Administrative & Operational Support
Support office operations, scheduling, event logistics, and stakeholder coordination.
Maintain organized records, contact databases, and engagement tracking systems.
Assist with purchasing, expense tracking, reimbursements, purchase orders, requisitions, and other administrative processes in accordance with university procedures.
Provide logistical support for meetings, events, travel, and official visits.
Perform additional duties and special assignments as needed.
Demonstrated growing network of professional relationships and with elected officials, government agencies, community leaders, and civic organizations.
Awareness of community organizations and landscape across Orange County and California.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and standard business applications.
Demonstrated knowledge of local, county, state, and/or federal government processes and public sector operations.
Familiarity with Orange County, California, and federal political landscapes, public-sector processes, and regional policy priorities.
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build trust and credibility across diverse constituencies.
Ability to work professionally in politically sensitive environments and support the university’s nonpartisan approach to government relations.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Bilingual or multilingual communication skills relevant to communities served by UC Irvine are valued.
Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment without much oversight.
Familiarity with artificial intelligence tools and emerging technologies for research, writing, project coordination, and administrative efficiency, with appropriate professional judgment.
Ability to exercise sound judgment, discretion, and confidentiality.
Familiarity with UC systems, public policy issues affecting higher education, healthcare, research, or economic development.
Ability to manage multiple assignments and deadlines with direction from senior staff
Basic knowledge of the institution, its mission, vision, goals, achievements, policies, and infrastructure.
Knowledge of basic concepts and principles of building and maintaining effective relations with a variety of constituencies.
Written, verbal and interpersonal skills, including political acumen to effectively represent the institution.
Analytical and critical thinking skills.
Organizational skills include meeting deadlines; and event planning skills.
Basic knowledge of public policy and the legislative process.
Applicable computer skills.
